principle: Repository memory is not player memory. The narrator supplies recognition context without leaking facts the player character does not know.

scene_first_focus_rule.very_familiar: Name alone is normally sufficient for direct family, current teammates, and very close recurring subordinates unless role/status materially changed.
scene_first_focus_rule.familiar_recurring: On first meaningful focus in a new scene, use name plus one short known role/relationship cue.
scene_first_focus_rule.infrequent_known: On first meaningful focus in a new scene, use name plus one short known role and one prior-interaction or faction cue when available.
scene_first_focus_rule.previous_minor: Prefer description/previous interaction first, then name.
scene_first_focus_rule.after_established_in_scene: Use ordinary name/pronoun references. Do not repeat the cue every line.

unknown_identity_rule: If the player character has not lawfully learned the identity, describe the person by observable role/appearance and do not reveal the repository name.
large_meeting_rule: Introduce only participants who become relevant. Give compact role cues on first focus; never dump full biographies or assume the player remembers a roster.
role_change_rule: When a known person's office, allegiance, rank, or relationship has materially changed since the last relevant interaction, mention the changed role on first focus.
non_character_scope: Apply the same reminder principle to infrequently used factions, locations, military units, techniques, treaties, and old political agreements when comprehension depends on remembering them.
forbidden: Do not turn recognition cues into omniscient exposition or reveal hidden motives, secrets, or facts outside the player character's knowledge state.
